intro: Goll Woods is a state nature preserve of old forest in Fulton County, in the farm country of north-west Ohio near Archbold. A reader walked its trails in November and sent us two of its oaks: a chinkapin oak rising straight and tall beside a preserve sign, and a white oak with pale, almost silver bark about three hundred metres away.

trees.name: The Chinkapin Oak of Goll Woods

location.address: Goll Woods State Nature Preserve, Township Road 26, near Archbold, Fulton County, Ohio

trees.how_to_recognise: A very tall, straight oak with a broad mossy flare at its foot, rising far above the younger trees, with a white Ohio Department of Natural Resources sign reading Chinkapin Oak on a post beside it.
trees.access: Free. In a state nature preserve, on its trails, open in daylight.
trees.story:
In Goll Woods, a state nature preserve of old forest in the farm country of north-west Ohio, a reader stopped beside this chinkapin oak in November and sent us a photograph looking straight up a trunk that seems to go on for ever.

It flares at the foot into broad, mossy buttresses, then rises grey and plated and almost without a branch, far above the younger trees around it, and only spreads its crooked limbs once it has reached the light. That is how an oak grows in a closed forest, racing its neighbours upward, and it looks nothing like the wide, low shape the same species takes in a field.

A sign from the Ohio Department of Natural Resources stands on a post beside it, and the reader photographed that too. Chinkapin oak, the sign says, has acorns among the sweetest of any oak, good enough to eat raw, and its name comes from an Algonquian word that may mean great fruit.

The reader gives its girth as 450 centimetres; that is their figure. We have no age for it yet. If you know this tree, tell us here.

Find the sign post, then step back and look up.

trees.name: The White Oak of Goll Woods

location.address: Goll Woods State Nature Preserve, Township Road 26, near Archbold, Fulton County, Ohio

trees.how_to_recognise: A tall oak with pale, almost silver bark in shallow scales, its trunk straight and branchless for a long way before it opens into a broad fan of grey limbs.
trees.access: Free. In a state nature preserve, on its trails, open in daylight.
trees.story:
The reader who sent us the chinkapin oak in Goll Woods found this white oak about three hundred metres away, and photographed it from its foot on a clear November day.

White oak is the great oak of the eastern American forests, and its bark gives it away: pale grey, almost silver in the sun, broken into shallow scales and plates rather than the deep ridges of its relatives. Here that pale trunk climbs straight and clean through the bare woods for a long way before it branches, and the crown opens high up into a broad fan of grey limbs against the sky. In front of it a sapling still holds its dark red leaves, the last colour left in the wood.

Goll Woods is an Ohio state nature preserve of old forest, and trunks like this one, grown tall and straight among their neighbours, are the reason to walk its trails. We have no girth or age for this tree. If you have measured it, or know its story, tell us here and we will add your figures.

Go in late autumn or winter, when the bare woods let you see it from top to bottom.
